body:
Controlled follow-up on the rdm_sampling_covariance cost bead, replacing the diagnosis I retracted. Every test below varies ONE driver with everything else fixed.

EXCLUDED BY MEASUREMENT - none of these produces anything near 9 s/node:

  accumulation/leak    12 sequential calls, ratio 1.05x, index-time correlation +0.084,
                       RSS net minus 30 MB
  frame size           same node from frames of 320/160/40/10 nodes: 1.771/1.283/1.320/1.673 s,
                       non-monotonic, 6 percent spread
  condition count q    q=2/4/6/8: 1.448/1.050/0.978/0.992 s - FLAT while D rises 1 to 28
  support size         support 5.8 -> 71.8, a 12x rise: cost FALLS, 1.180 to 0.653 s
  feature count P      P=100/200/400/800 at fixed support: 1.22x across an 8x rise
  target policy        null 0.304 s vs plugin 0.195 s - plugin is faster

At my closest synthetic match to the exemplar - q=8, P=400, mean support 41, a real
compile_frame(searchlights(4.0)) - a sweep runs at 0.088 s/node against the exemplar's 9 s/node.
A factor of about one hundred, and none of the six parameters above accounts for any of it.

SO THE COST IS NOT IN THE COVARIANCE MATHEMATICS. Everything that shapes the Eq. 13 computation
has been varied across its plausible range and none of it matters. That excludes a large surface
and points at the data path: NIfTI-backed sources and real block reads, lm_relation_fit over real
timeseries, or per-call source access that in-memory matrices never exercise. Profiling one
exemplar call would settle it in minutes; I cannot, without the prepared Haxby data.

ONE SUBSTANTIVE DATUM ON THE PROPOSED FIX. The bead's first fix shape is a precompute-once shared
object. That mechanism already exists as residual_strategy = 'shared_pair_statistics'. It is
reachable on a real compile_frame - my earlier attempt was refused only because a hand-built
additive_frame has no support index, and the message says exactly that. But it does not pay off
at these sizes:

  1 node     node_local 0.404 s/node   shared_pair_statistics 0.764 s/node
  10 nodes   node_local 0.088 s/node   shared_pair_statistics 0.162 s/node

About 1.8x SLOWER per node at both. It may turn positive at 577 nodes with 50-voxel spheres -
the regime I cannot reach - but the proposed fix may already be implemented and simply not yet
worth using, and that is worth knowing before building a second one.

Opposite of the original hypothesis, and worth flagging: per-node cost FALLS sharply as a sweep
proceeds here, 0.404 s at one node to 0.088 s across ten. Something already amortizes. The
exemplar sees a flat 9 s/node over 577 nodes, so whatever amortizes here does not amortize there.

CAVEAT, given my record on this bead: all synthetic, all in memory. The firm result is a negative
- the analytic parameters do not explain the cost. I am not offering a positive diagnosis this time.
